title: Same molecule, Different Knowledge: Cross-Identifier Binding Failures in LLMs For chemistry
abstract: arXiv:2610.30903v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Chemical AI workflows routinely represent the same molecule through multiple co-referring identifiers, including trivial names, IUPAC names, and SMILES, implicitly assuming that these representations provide interchangeable access to an LLM's knowledge. To test this assumption, we first introduce a controlled benchmark and show that it does not hold. Across foundation models spanning 7B to 72B parameters, even chemistry-specialized models, co-referring molecular identifiers consistently expose different subsets of the model's knowledge. We then conduct a series of controlled behavioral, representational, and causal analyses to characterize this failure. We show that even when a model can identify a molecule from its SMILES and retrieve a fact through the corresponding name, the same fact can remain inaccessible directly from SMILES. translated_title: 同一分子，不同的知识：化学领域大语言模型中的跨标识符绑定失效
translated_abstract: 化学AI工作流程通常通过多个互指标识符来表示同一分子，包括俗名、IUPAC名称和SMILES，并隐含地假设这些表示形式能够以可互换的方式访问大语言模型的知识。为了验证这一假设，我们首先引入了一个受控基准测试，结果表明该假设并不成立。在参数规模从7B到72B的基础模型中，即使是化学专业模型，互指的分子标识符始终暴露出模型知识的不同子集。随后，我们进行了一系列受控的行为、表征和因果分析来刻画这种失败现象。我们证明，即使模型能够通过SMILES识别出某个分子，并通过相应的名称检索到某个事实，同一事实却可能无法直接从SMILES中获取。我们将这种现象称为“跨标识符绑定失效”。对内部表征的进一步分析……
tldr: 该论文通过受控基准和行为、表征、因果分析，首次揭示并验证了大语言模型中“跨标识符绑定失效”现象，即同一分子的俗名、IUPAC名称和SMILES等互指标识符所激活的模型知识子集并不互通。
